liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dire Wolf** (2 reviews): A great early version of Dire Wolf, one of the reviewer's favorites; Jerry sings lead on Dire Wolf here instead of Bob, who had sung it before [10][17]
- **Hard To Handle** (2 reviews): Garcia plays pedal steel on Hard To Handle, which the reviewer loves; Hard To Handle is a gem, with Jerry on pedal steel [7][13]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): One of the best Dupree's ever, thanks to the drums and Garcia's vocals [10]
- **Silver Threads & Golden Needles** (1 review): Silver Threads features Jerry on pedal steel and is called a gem [13]
- **Alligator** (1 review): The long jam following Alligator is a nice stretch of the show [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Story of a Brick**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-07-11.127258.sbd.kaplan.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 94 min; rated 2.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Light EQ was applied to the included audience segment [1]
- **gd69-07-11.sbd.hanno.4644.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 15 songs; 98 min; rated 3.43/5 by 21 [2]. Said about its sound: The recording is kick-ass but has a hissy quality; On the first night Jerry played steel and the sound was not great; The tape has fantastic drum sound [7][8][10][11][13][14][16]
- **gd1969-07-11.153553.aud.flac1644**: audience recording; 8 songs; 49 min [6]. Said about its sound: It sounds like the audience portions of 4644/4645 but with more material, though with many dropouts and anomalies [6]
- **gd1969-07-11.123417.sbd.latvala.lee.smith.flac24**: soundboard; 14 songs; 89 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- The reviewer's band Tribe opened for the Dead and Joe Cocker on this night and the next [8]
- The reviewer was 15 and attended with his girlfriend; it was their first Dead show, and Tribe played [9]
- Bobby makes corny jokes at the start of the set [14]
- The reviewer believes Phil Lesh is the voice interrupting Jerry, though not certain [15]
- Bobby tells stories during the intro to kill time [16]
- The following night the sound was great, and the opening band was invited to sit on stage [8]
- The next night's show has a truly great Dark Star [11]
- The sound is nicer than many 1970 board recordings, which are hit or miss [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-07-11.127258.sbd.kaplan.flac16**: transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: Recording Info: SBD Master Cassette > DAT (Panasonic 3700) [1]. Also: This source is MSC direct to DAT, skipping the extra analog cassette generations; The audience patch covers Alligator into 1:36 of Drums, from audience master via low-gen reel and cassette to CD [1]
- **gd69-07-11.sbd.hanno.4644.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Hanno Bunjes, Uli, Julian; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [2]. Also: The soundboard cassette breaks off during High Time; side B starts in the drums after Alligator and ends during Lovelight; The circulating audience tape runs from Alligator into The Other One before cutting off [2]
- **gd1969-07-11.153553.aud.flac1644**: taped by from collection of Rich Petrunis.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 09/2021; source: Unknown mono AUD from collection of Rich Petrunis. [6]. Also: This audience source derives from mix-tapes containing parts of both nights [6]
- **gd1969-07-11.123417.sbd.latvala.lee.smith.flac24**: taped by Dick Latvala, Pat Lee; transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD Recording Info: Pat Lee from Dick Latvala 1985 Technics 1506> Yamaha K2000 MSC > C > C > CD; Transfer Info: Mastered via the Apogee Mini Me(24/96) > Mini… [3]
